earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog refs for Buna (bvn) are wordlists/surveys only (Laycock checklists, Sanders & Sanders 1980 Marienberg survey); no grammar or phonology exists.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Buna language' (read online 2026-09-17).
sources.note: Morphology stub only (four noun classes, concord examples cited to Foley 2018); nothing on phonology or stress.

sources.citation: SIL PNG. 2007-2013 [Internet Archive copy 2015-05-12]. PNG Language Resources: Buna information [bvn]. Ukarumpa: SIL-PNG. ('Language resources: Nothing yet available or materials are not yet processed.')
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: no phonology content -- catalogue page listing no resources.

sources.citation: Foley, W.A. 2005. Linguistic prehistory in the Sepik-Ramu basin. In Pawley et al. (eds), Papuan Pasts, PL 572: 109-144.
sources.note: Buna mentioned once (Murik silent trade with inland Buna); no linguistic data.

sources.citation: Wurm, Stephen A. 1986. Grammatical decay in Papuan languages. In Papers in New Guinea Linguistics No. 24 (Pacific Linguistics A-70), 207-211. Canberra: Australian National University. (Buna: p. 210.)
sources.note: Nothing: the paper is about loss of morphological complexity (Kiwai, Buna, Murik, Mountain Arapesh, Ayiwo); no phonology, and the words stress/tone/accent/pitch do not occur. Its one Buna paragraph reports that Kirschbaum's 12 noun classes were not found by Laycock in 1971.

sources.citation: Sanders, Arden G. & Joy Sanders. 1980. Defining the centres of the Marienberg language family. PL A-56: 171-196.
sources.note: Nothing; lexicostatistics and sociolinguistic survey, 'the data was not phonemicised' (p.172); Appendix C gives Buna pronouns/verb prefixes only.

sources.citation: Greenhill, S. TransNewGuinea.org: Buna (Torricelli) wordlist, source SIL 1975 Murik survey.
sources.note: Wordlist only, no stress marks, no statement.

sources.citation: Laycock, D.C. 1975. The Torricelli Phylum. In Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study 1, PL C-38: 767-780 (Buna sec. 2.12, pp. 774-775).
sources.note: Phylum-level phonological characterisation (p.769) has no stress statement; Buna section only quotes Kirschbaum 1922 on noun classes; nothing on Buna stress.

sources.citation: Laycock, D.C. 1973. Sepik Languages: Checklist and Preliminary Classification. Pacific Linguistics B-25. Canberra: ANU. Entry 51 BUNA, pp. 16-17.
sources.note: Nothing; villages, test list DCL71 (Taturi/Mambel), note that Kirschbaum's grammar was burnt at Kambot, noun classes unconfirmed in 1971.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1965. The Ndu language family (Sepik District, New Guinea) (Pacific Linguistics C-1). Canberra: ANU. [Bibliography annotation of Friederici 1912: '[Buna, Boikin, Angoram, Murik and Kobar * @]' = scattered lexical items + distribution; fieldwork log 'Marienberg SVD Buna W 1960 Jan.' = Laycock's own Buna wordlist of January 1960.]
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: Nothing on Buna phonology; Buna appears only in lists, a population table and bibliography annotations.

sources.citation: Voegelin, C.F. & F.M. Voegelin. 1965. Languages of the World: Indo-Pacific Fascicle Five. Anthropological Linguistics 7(9). (ERIC ED010365.)
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: no phonology content -- a one-sentence demographic listing (after Capell/Laycock); nothing on sounds, stress or tone.

sources.citation: Kirschbaum, Franz. 1926. Miscellanea aus Neuguinea, IV. Der Urstamm der Buna (Marienberg). Anthropos 21: 274-277 (Buna pp. 276-277).
sources.note: Nothing; totem legends and 'bis jetzt habe ich zwoelf Nominalklassen feststellen koennen'. His Buna grammar MS was never published (reported burnt in WWII by Laycock).

sources.citation: Kirschbaum, Franz. 1921-1922. Sprache[n]- und Kulturgruppierungen in Deutsch-Neuguinea. Anthropos 16-17: 1052-1053.
sources.note: Nothing; only remarks on Buna's nine noun classes and object suffixes.

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2018. The languages of the Sepik-Ramu basin and environs. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area: A Comprehensive Guide, 197-432. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton (Torricelli / Marienberg section).
